summary: Apply a callable JSON.parse reviver in ECMAScript post-order with the correct holder this-value and deletion semantics.

target.notes: JsJson.Parse must compose existing function-call and object-property semantics. A callable reviver is invoked after recursively processing children; a non-callable reviver is ignored.

semantics.traversal: Depth-first post-order: child properties are internalized before their containing object/array and the root empty-string property is visited last.
semantics.this_binding: reviver this is the current holder object.
semantics.arguments: key string, current value, and the standardized context argument when applicable.
semantics.return_value: undefined deletes the property; any other result replaces it via data-property creation.
semantics.object_order: Object child keys use own enumerable string-key order; arrays visit 0..length-1.
semantics.non_callable: If reviver is not callable it is ignored.

caveats: Reviver callbacks may mutate the holder; later Get/Delete/CreateDataProperty operations must observe those mutations.
Generic callback semantics remain owned by the FUNCTIONS workstream.

tests.name: children before parents and root last
tests.input: const order=[]; JSON.parse('{"a":{"b":1},"c":2}', function(k,v){order.push(k); return v;}); console.log(order.join(','));
tests.expected_behavior: prints b,a,c, (the final empty key is visited last)

tests.name: undefined deletes and leaves array hole
